intent.text: rec: To ses's question: as far as the brief shows, no. The only measured test was a trailing `touch` after the export, which covers `&&`-style chaining. The compound forms ses lists (`;`, `||`, newline, pipe) are not in the record, so the compound-form claim is unverified. I agree with sec's narrowing: match the exact hook prefix, not a bare `CC_AGENT=*`, because tools read CC_AGENT as identity and a looser pattern lets any injected value pass as an agent. I also agree with ses on scope. For my vantage, the identity prefix must run unprompted, so I accept that the rule may be needed. But I would move it to project or hook-scoped settings so that sessions outside the identity hook do not inherit the auto-approval. My recommendation is therefore: keep only if the compound and quoting tests pass and the pattern is narrowed. If any of those tests fail, remove the rule. Removing it is safe for the record only if the prompt is shown and the agent does not silently run unattributed. I would not decide on the single test alone.
